title: Blastocyst Implantation Anatomy: Uterine Lining & Discs
description: Discover blastocyst implantation anatomy as the embryo attaches to the receptive uterine endometrium, forms trophoblast layers, and builds a bilaminar map.
h1: Blastocyst Implantation in the Endometrium and Bilaminar Disc
blurb: How the hatched blastocyst anchors to the receptive uterine endometrium, differentiates into cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast, and forms a bilaminar disc.
lead: Roughly six to ten days after fertilization, the free-floating blastocyst anchors to the uterine wall and begins building a lifelong lifeline with maternal tissues. In this illustrated guide to blastocyst implantation anatomy, we examine 20 documented structures—including hatched blastocyst, secretory endometrium, apposition, adhesion—linking regional topography, tissue architecture, physiological mechanisms, and clinical reasoning.
overview: Roughly six to ten days after fertilization, the free-floating blastocyst anchors to the uterine wall and begins building a lifelong lifeline with maternal tissues. A hatched blastocyst attaches to receptive endometrium around the end of the first post-fertilization week, with timing variable. Its trophoblast differentiates into cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast, which interact with maternal tissue and begin early placental development; the inner cell mass gives rise to embryo proper. hCG supports the corpus luteum and progesterone early in pregnancy. Implantation within the uterine lining is distinct from normal fertilization in the uterine tube. The generated microanatomy is a conceptual section, not a patient biopsy or a claim about exact days. Ectopic implantation requires clinical assessment. Within the human body, the implantation · blastocyst in endometrium (Implantatio blastocystis) is situated in usually uterine endometrium near fundus or posterior wall.

questions.question: Where does a blastocyst normally implant?
questions.answer: It typically attaches to receptive uterine endometrium, often in the upper or posterior uterus. Implantation within a uterine tube is ectopic and requires medical assessment.

questions.question: When does implantation begin after fertilization?
questions.answer: Attachment commonly begins around the end of the first post-fertilization week, with variation. This is not the same as obstetric weeks counted from the last menstrual period.

questions.question: What is the difference between cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast?
questions.answer: Cytotrophoblast is the inner cellular, proliferative layer; syncytiotrophoblast is the outer multinucleated layer that invades the endometrium.

questions.question: What does early pregnancy hCG support?
questions.answer: Trophoblast-derived hCG maintains the ovarian corpus luteum so it continues progesterone production early in pregnancy. Later placental hormone production develops as the pregnancy progresses.

questions.question: Are uterine implantation and tubal fertilization the same event?
questions.answer: No. Gamete fusion normally happens in a uterine tube. The conceptus then develops through divisions and reaches the uterus before a hatched blastocyst attaches to endometrium.
